CHIEF COMPLAINT
Upper respiratory infection

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrew is a 59-year-old male presenting with upper respiratory infection symptoms. Patient reports that approximately one week ago while doing yard work and landscaping, he began experiencing fatigue and shortness of breath. He notes that he was not wearing masks frequently and believes he caught a cold that subsequently worsened. Shortness of breath occurs primarily with exertion, such as lifting and carrying heavy bags of soil. Patient denies currently coughing up sputum but anticipates this may develop. He reports feeling slightly warm but attributed this to exertion rather than fever. Patient also notes bilateral elbow pain and knee fatigue, which he attributes primarily to the physical labor involved in landscaping. Patient has received both COVID vaccines. Denies seasonal allergies. Denies nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for fatigue, shortness of breath with exertion, bilateral elbow pain, and knee fatigue. Denies fever, productive cough, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and seasonal allergies.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin (dose to be increased)
Lisinopril 20 mg daily

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is employed during the week. Wife encourages participation in barre classes for relaxation. Recently engaged in landscaping and yard work. Inconsistent monitoring of blood glucose and blood pressure on weekends versus weekdays. Diet generally controlled except for occasional indulgences at social gatherings.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Normal, no fever
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, strong heart sounds
Lungs: Scattered rhonchi bilaterally that clear with cough
Extremities: Mild edema of lower extremities noted
Musculoskeletal: Bilateral elbow pain on palpation

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No airspace disease, no pneumonia
Hemoglobin A1c: 8.0 (elevated; goal 6-7)
COVID test: Pending

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Upper respiratory infection/Viral syndrome: Likely viral etiology. COVID test to be sent to rule out COVID-19. Patient counseled that symptoms should resolve in a couple of days. Prescribed Robitussin for cough. Advised to take ibuprofen and acetaminophen as needed for fever and discomfort. Patient instructed to contact if symptoms worsen.

2. Depression: Currently managed without pharmacotherapy. Patient reports doing well with support from wife and barre classes. Offered option of starting medication or psychotherapy referral; patient prefers to reassess in a few months.

3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Hemoglobin A1c elevated at 8.0. Increased metformin to 1000 mg twice daily. Repeat hemoglobin A1c to be checked in four months to assess response to therapy adjustment.

4. Hypertension: Currently well-controlled on lisinopril 20 mg daily. Continue current medication. Lisinopril refill provided. Lipid panel ordered.

Follow-up appointment scheduled in four months.
